chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The pregnant woman, close (to giving birth), and the breast-feeder with little milk, there is no blame upon them if they break (the fast) during the month of Ramadan, because they are not able to tolerate the fast, and upon them is that they should give in charity, each one of them, for each day they break the fast therein, with a mudd of food, and upon them both is the making up (qada) for each day they broke the fast therein, which they will make up afterwards.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim,
from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.الْحَامِلُ الْمُقْرِبُ: The pregnant woman close to giving birth
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ: With a mudd (a unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for pregnant women and nursing mothers who cannot fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *rukhas* (divine concessions) for pregnant women near term and nursing mothers with insufficient milk, prioritizing their health and the child's welfare over strict fasting. It specifies a dual obligation: paying *fidya* (one mudd of food per day) as compensation for the inability to fast, alongside the requirement to perform *qada* (make-up fasting) later, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these categories are not permanently exempt but conditionally excused.
